title: Lane Bryant vs. Lands' End chinos: Two low-synthetic options for a size 20 short travel pant
summary: A recent shopper wanted a size 20 short pant with real pockets, little or no polyester, and a polished shape. These two current chinos meet that brief differently in sizing, fabric, closure, and length.
author: Curvy& Editorial

sections.heading: A useful pants search starts with constraints, not a brand list
paragraphs: In a recent r/PlusSizeFashion thread, a US size 20 shopper preparing for travel wanted short-length pants, front and back pockets, no polyester, and a polished look at under $80. The discussion is useful because each condition removes options that might otherwise look suitable in a broad plus-size search. The shopper later reported buying two pairs from Lane Bryant, while replies also discussed Lands' End and the difficulty of being between sizes.

Two current products make a practical comparison: Lane Bryant's Pull-On Super-Soft Straight Leg Chino and Lands' End's Mid Rise Classic Straight Leg Chino Ankle Pant. Both avoid polyester, include multiple pockets, use a mid rise, and publish a 27-inch option for the relevant plus-size shopper. They differ substantially in fabric, closure, and how that 27-inch length is categorized.

sections.heading: The size charts nearly align at 20, but the labels do not
paragraphs: Lane Bryant's pants chart assigns size 20 to a 42-inch waist and 50.5-inch low hip. Lands' End's plus chart assigns 20W to a 42–43-inch waist and 50-inch hip. On paper, those body ranges are close enough to form a sensible cross-brand starting point, but Lane Bryant calls the size 20 while Lands' End uses 20W.

That similarity is not proof of identical finished garments. Neither comparison should skip rise placement or the difference between a pull-on waist and a fixed fly front. Measure your natural waist and fullest low hip, then compare a successful mid-rise pant. If your waist and hip point to different sizes, prioritize the area the garment cannot comfortably negotiate and use the return policy as part of the decision.

sections.heading: Lane Bryant offers a softer pull-on build and an explicit short length
paragraphs: Lane Bryant's current chino is 52% cotton, 46% lyocell, and 2% spandex. It has a covered elastic waistband with a drawstring, a faux fly, belt loops, two front and two back pockets, and a straight leg described as slim from the waist to mid-thigh. The published inseams are 27 inches for short, 29 inches for regular, and 32 inches for long; the page lists size 20S among the selectable variants.

Editorially, this is the more forgiving travel option when a fixed fly becomes uncomfortable during long periods of sitting or when a drawstring helps stabilize the waist. Lyocell usually contributes softness and drape, while the small spandex content adds some give. Those material cues do not guarantee a wrinkle-free pant or a perfect waistband, so assess how the fabric looks after sitting before making it the only polished pant in a suitcase.

The tradeoff is visual and structural. A pull-on waist and faux fly may feel more casual than a traditional chino closure, and the slim fit through mid-thigh may be the limiting point for fuller thighs even when waist and hip match the chart.

sections.heading: Lands' End uses crisper cotton and calls the same inseam plus length
paragraphs: The Lands' End ankle chino is 98% cotton and 2% spandex. It uses a hook-and-bar closure with a zip fly and belt loops, plus front pockets, back button pockets, and a coin pocket. The straight leg tapers slightly at the ankle. Published inseams are 28 inches regular, 25.5 petite, 30 tall, and 27 plus.

For a 20W shopper who needs approximately 27 inches, the plus version already lands at the target length even though it is not labeled short. This is a reminder to compare inches rather than filter names: one brand's short and another brand's plus can reach the same nominal inseam. The Lands' End option is the stronger match when a conventional chino front, higher cotton percentage, and a crisper trouser appearance matter most.

It is less adjustable at the waist than Lane Bryant's pull-on design. A 2% spandex twill may flex, but the hook-and-bar closure still has to sit comfortably after a meal and through a travel day. If the waist is between chart ranges, do not assume the fabric will replace needed ease.

sections.heading: Which pair better satisfies the travel brief?
paragraphs: Start with Lane Bryant if comfort at the waist, an adjustable drawstring, and a clearly labeled short option are the priorities. Start with Lands' End if you want a more traditional fly-front chino, the highest possible cotton content between these two, and a 27-inch plus inseam. Both product pages were listed under the shopper's $80 ceiling at research time, but prices, promotions, colors, and stock can change.

Before removing tags, load the pockets, sit for twenty minutes, climb stairs, and test the intended shoes. Check whether the pocket bags pull open, the waistband folds, the rise migrates, or the hem catches on footwear. Lane Bryant allows eligible online purchases to be returned in a store or by shipment, but shipping charges are nonrefundable and exchanges by return shipment require a new order. Lands' End currently charges $6.95 for Happy Returns or mail refunds to the original payment method, waives that fee for eligible merchandise credit within 90 days, and offers free returns in its own stores. Confirm the current terms and final-sale status at checkout.
bullets: Compare the 27-inch inseams with a pant worn at a similar rise.
Measure thigh and front rise in addition to waist and low hip.
Pack the closure you can comfortably wear while seated for hours.
Keep a second polished bottom if the trip begins before the return window can absorb an exchange.

researchNote: This comparison answers an August 2026 community request and checks current product construction, fiber content, inseams, body charts, pockets, and return terms on official Lane Bryant and Lands' End pages. The two garments are starting points, not guarantees; fit can vary with waist-to-hip ratio, thigh shape, rise preference, fabric batch, and desired ease.
